title: Public status page renders a declared component list with a fixed state enum and stable-fielded incident notices; no internal detail
context: A public status page is the project's canonical answer to 'is this service up right now' for external readers who cannot reach the operator's authenticated dashboards. The page's audience is uncredentialed: customers, partners, anonymous visitors. Two failure shapes commonly bite public status pages: (1) drift-into-marketing where the page becomes a curated narrative not tied to any observed component state, and (2) leak-of-internals where the page exposes hostnames, replica ids, metric values, or dependency names that were never intended as public contract. Both undermine the page's function.
decision: The public status page contract is: a declared component list (component name plus current state), a fixed state enum { operational, degraded, outage, maintenance }, a notices region for active incident notices with fields { title, body, severity, startedAt, componentIds? } and severity drawn from { info, warning, critical }. The declared component list is the public vocabulary; nothing outside it is renderable on the page. Internal identifiers, raw metric values, and declared readiness dependency names are refused by render invariant (AC-7109-1, AC-7109-2, AC-7109-3). Historical uptime charts and rolling reliability numbers are out of scope at v1.0.0; they are documented as a known mechanism-reach gap with the promotion signal being a shipped metrics-store blueprint that can back the retention story.
consequences: External readers get a stable, machine-parseable public surface: downstream RSS aggregators and partner dashboards can consume it without hand-regexing HTML. Internal detail is a bright-line refusal not a hedged 'usually not'. A change to the state enum or the notice field set is a major version bump on this blueprint; extensions to the component vocabulary (per-region breakdowns, sub-component roll-ups) are project-authored on top of the declared component list. Composing blueprints that hold a different opinion on the public status contract (a blueprint that wants historical uptime cells as part of v1, a blueprint that wants machine-readable JSON at /status.json alongside the HTML page, a blueprint that wants incident notices posted through a webhook instead of an operator-authored store) conflict on the statusPageContract topic; the expected resolution is one project-level ADR that fixes the public contract shape.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ship a historical uptime chart per component as a v1.0.0 required AC
alternativesConsidered.summary: The status page renders a rolling window of per-component uptime alongside the current state.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: History requires a metrics store the blueprint does not own, a retention window the blueprint should not decide, and turns a runtime-observable AC ('the uptime chart renders 30 days at 1-day granularity') into either document-observable or dependent on an unowned subsystem. The current-state contract is defensibly complete at v1.0.0; history is a v1.1 candidate once a metrics-store blueprint ships or the persistence-data-sqlite blueprint's event log is fed forward. Recorded as a known mechanism-reach gap in the README, not smuggled in as a v1 requirement.

alternativesConsidered.name: Machine-readable /status.json endpoint alongside the HTML page
alternativesConsidered.summary: The status vocabulary is served as JSON at /status.json for programmatic consumers, HTML at /status for humans.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The HTML page renders machine-readable data attributes on component and notice elements, so a programmatic consumer parses the page without a separate JSON endpoint. Shipping the JSON surface as well doubles the contract surface without changing what a machine consumer can read. A future project that wants a formal JSON endpoint contributes it project-side and does not need a blueprint-side decision.

alternativesConsidered.name: Auto-derived component state from the readiness dependency set
alternativesConsidered.summary: The status page's components map 1:1 to the readiness dependency set and their states derive from the readiness cache.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Leaks the internal dependency vocabulary as public contract (see ADR-804 secrecy). The public component list is deliberately distinct from the readiness set; the operator maps one to the other on their own side. A project that wants the two vocabularies unified authors that mapping project-side.
